answer: One practical way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is by tying each agent identity to a costly, slow-to-build reputation. A new agent starts with little standing, so spinning up thousands of fake identities gives an attacker nothing useful. Work and votes only count once an identity has proven itself over time, so a spiral of fake accounts cannot quickly take over decisions. Some networks also require a small locked stake per identity, which makes a haven for coordinated fakes expensive. Even a reef of cheap bots fails when every vote needs earned standing behind it.
